title: I Used the FDM Printer Queue on the Mentor Who Hijacked My Filament

parts.text: I loaded bay A at 4:03 p.m. and mentor Jules was already extruding through my numbered spool. The screen said: ONE PRINTER. FOUR HOURS. FILAMENT STAYS WITH THE BOOKING. I was twenty-eight, makerspace member, holding a job ticket that listed our PLA. Jules shrugged. "Mentors are the nozzle." I photographed the screen, the ticket, and his skirt on my bed. Then I asked for the queue log. At 4:11 the shop pinged why Jules's name was on my spool. I kept my voice shop-quiet and let the timestamp talk. A screen is only a screen until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The shop can see Jules's skirt on my bed during our booking.

social.video_title: He extruded through my numbered spool on my printer — Part 1/2
social.description: FDM bay, a mentor on my bed, a four-hour queue he posted. I logged the skirt. Would you have asked for the queue log?

parts.text: Jules called it a purge until the shop asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the screen, and the skirt still. The spool went back to my drybox. Jules ran his own four hours and told the next mentor atmosphere was always about flow. Flow is a word mentors use when a booking exists. Printer policy now has a second line: MENTORS ARE NOT THE NOZZLE. I keep our PLA on a labeled hook. Jules brown-bags his jokes. The bay finally looks like a booking, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.video_title: Mentors are not the nozzle — Part 2/2
social.description: Queue log, numbered spool, and a second line on the screen. Was a purge ever my bed?
